items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: The interviewee identifies himself as 'H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux'. The 'PERSON TO JUDGE' is the same individual.

ctx.x: What's your name anyway? My name is Al Rose. Is that your full name? No, my full name is H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux. My God. I thought it was E. Albert Rose for years. Well, I actually did use that name for years for complex reasons. Where were you born? I was born in New Orleans in a 2-0 infirmary on February 3rd, 1916. Makes me 59 years old today. Just,

I'm not taking anything in any particular order. Okay. Other than happy birthday. Thank you, Richard. Oh, I didn't tell you my name. My name is Dick Allen, commonly known as Richard. Enough of this feeble attempt at you, and I'm tired. I interviewed Russell last night. Two hours of tennis and one hour of interview with Russell. It's an hour and a half. What I did with Russell. items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: The interviewee states: 'My full name is H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux'. The person to judge is the interviewee himself.

ctx.x: It's too early for me. And my name is John Perhanis, and I'm from Minneapolis, studying at the Jazz Archives at Tulane for a period of six weeks here, in which time I met Al Rose, who lives in New Orleans. And I should mention that I met him through one of his books called Storyville. Which, when I picked it up in the bookstore, fascinated me so much that I went out and bought it, which I could not afford to do, but I did anyway. And then I called Al Rose, and we got to know each other a little bit. Al, there's…

Well, the name itself is real, of course, but it's much truncated. My full name is H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux, and it is, as you might suspect, an old New Orleans name. And I am myself a representative of the seventh generation of the family in New Orleans. Is that a Creole, of Creole? Oh, yes. It is a Creole name.
And is Al Rose a pen name, as it were?
